from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear transformations stretch or rotate space.",
            "Most vectors change their direction.",
            "Special vectors stay on their span.",
            "These are the eigen-directions.",
            "Visualize stretching rubber along an axis."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition: Stretching vs. Rotating", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        rubber_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rubber.svg")
        
        # Setup base objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.65)
        self.add(axes)
        
        # Add rubber icon to axes
        self.place_in_area(rubber_icon, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(rubber_icon)

        # 1. Rotating vector
        vec_rot = Vector([1, 1], color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(vec_rot, 'D3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # 2. Stretching vector
        vec_stretch = Vector([1, 0], color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(vec_stretch, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(rubber_icon), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.add(vec_rot)
        self.play(Rotate(vec_rot, angle=PI, about_point=axes.c2p(0, 0)), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.add(vec_stretch)
        # Add eigen-line visual representation
        eigen_line = Line(start=axes.c2p(-3, 0), end=axes.c2p(3, 0), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(eigen_line), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        both = VGroup(vec_rot, vec_stretch)
        self.play(Indicate(both), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(axes.animate.apply_matrix([[2, 0], [0, 1]]), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Constructing the Eigenbasis", [
            "Eigenvectors can form an eigenbasis.",
            "The matrix A becomes diagonal.",
            "This simplifies complex calculations."
        ])
        
        # Setup basis vectors
        e1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        e2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color=WHITE)
        basis = VGroup(e1, e2)
        self.place_in_area(basis, 'B3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(basis))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform basis (Matrix A applied)
        new_e1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5 + UP*0.5, color="#FF0000")
        new_e2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT*0.5 + UP*2.0, color="#FF0000")
        new_basis = VGroup(new_e1, new_e2)
        self.place_in_area(new_basis, 'B3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.95)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(basis, new_basis))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Identify spanning space
        span = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(span, 'B3', 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(span))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis: The Geometry of Linear Transformations

sections.title: The Intuition: Stretching vs. Rotating
sections.content: Introduce linear transformations as 'stretching' space. Most vectors change direction when transformed. However, some special vectors stay on their original 'span' (line). These are the 'eigen-directions'.
sections.example: Visualize a grid of rubber being pulled diagonally. Most arrows point to new directions, but the arrows pointing along the pull axis remain stuck on their original lines.

sections.title: Defining the Eigen-Pair
sections.content: Define the equation Av = λv. 'A' is the transformation, 'v' is the eigenvector (the direction that doesn't change), and 'λ' (lambda) is the eigenvalue (the scalar factor of stretch or shrink).
sections.example: Imagine a 2D robot arm. If the arm moves, an eigenvector is the 'axis' of the arm that only changes length, not orientation. λ > 1 means it stretches; λ < 1 means it shrinks; λ = -1 means it flips.

sections.title: Constructing the Eigenbasis
sections.content: If we have enough linearly independent eigenvectors, they form an 'eigenbasis'. In this coordinate system, the matrix A becomes a simple diagonal matrix, making complex transformations computationally trivial.
sections.example: Think of a chaotic cloud of bird migration. If we use the 'eigenbasis' (the primary paths of travel), the complex matrix describing the flock becomes a simple set of independent growth rates.

sections.title: Visual Summary & Practical Application
sections.content: Connect the math to the 'Eigenface' concept. By finding the eigenvectors of a face database, we can represent any face as a combination of 'eigen-features' rather than raw pixels.
sections.example: A security system identifying a face by assigning weights to 'eigen-noses' and 'eigen-eyes' instead of analyzing every single pixel.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The scatter plot visualization overlaps with the horizontal and vertical axes, causing visual clutter in the center of the frame. Fix: self.place_in_area(scatter_plot, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=6, object=scatter_plot)
issues.resolution_note: Clutter addressed by using face.svg in area B2-E5.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The grid labels (A1-F6) are visually redundant and clutter the area intended for the SVM classification boundary example. Fix: self.place_in_area(grid_points, 'B2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=7, object=grid_points)
issues.resolution_note: Grid clutter removed.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The lecture text is too close to the left edge, reducing readability when objects appear on the right. Fix: self.place_in_area(lecture_text, 'A1', 'D1', scale_factor=0.9) (line=1, object=lecture_text)
issues.resolution_note: Lecture text readability maintained within layout.
